Dev log

Commander Wren

One commander leads on the Terra table: Wren, enhanced infantry on foot in powered armor, a scout drone hovering at her shoulder. She is the only commander on this battlefield — the red force opposing her is a commander-less mechanized column, richer and fielding an extra recon, whose only eyes are steel. Wren's gift is seeing the table before the enemy does. Her aura reaches 2 hexes: foot units inside it capture faster and hold cover like veterans.

How to play

One Terra skirmish against the CPU, on the miniature table.

Turn: tap one of your blue miniatures, tap a softly lit hex to move, then tap a red enemy in range: the filled red pips above it preview the HP it would lose, and the smaller hollow pips the counterattack it would deal back. Tap it again, or tap the crosshair beside it, to strike. Indirect units (Artillery, Rockets, deployed Siege) may move and fire in the same turn. The Siege must deploy in place before it can fire its long-range splash shot, and cannot move while deployed.

Capture: park Infantry, Mech or Wren herself on a property and choose Capture. Capturing takes two turns, faster inside Wren's aura. Towns, factories and the relay pay income each turn; factories build new units. Capturing the enemy HQ wins at once.

Win three ways: capture the enemy HQ, rout every enemy unit, or capture the central relay and hold it for 3 of your turns.

Surround: each of your units standing beside the target beyond the first adds about +10% damage and blunts the counterattack. When a strike is armed, each supporting unit shows a gold pip and the target's outline deepens; a target whose pips pulse is about to be destroyed.

Fog: unexplored table lies in shadow, and sight on this table is short: most units see only 2 hexes, medium tanks and battle copters 3, and the recon — the army's dedicated eyes — 4. Explored ground stays dim and shows no units. Forest hides a unit unless an enemy stands next to it; hills and forests block sight lines. Finding the enemy before it finds you is the game: push recons and drones forward, and expect the red column to be doing the same with its recons. Wren's drones are the exception: whatever a drone can reach with its sensors is fully revealed, forest or no forest.

Commander Wren: only the blue army fields a commander. Wren is enhanced infantry on foot: she crosses forest, hills and rough ground at foot cost, takes infantry cover and forest hiding, is targeted as infantry rather than as a vehicle, can capture, and keeps commander-grade strength. Her aura reaches 2 hexes: foot units inside it capture faster, and infantry holding forest or a property inside it gains extra cover. If she is downed, she returns at her HQ after 3 turns at reduced strength, and while she is down no new drones can launch. The red column has no commander, no aura and no drones — it compensates with extra funds and an extra recon.

Drones: tap Wren and choose the drone icon to launch a scout drone; launching is her action for the turn. She may keep at most two drones aloft. A drone flies 6 hexes over any ground, cannot attack, and cannot end its move on an occupied hex. Its sensors fully reveal everything within 3 hexes, including units hidden in forest, which makes it the best way to learn a new table. It is fragile: a single hit from anything that can target air brings it down, and anti-air guns are its natural counter. For now her drones only scout. As Wren gains levels in later battles, her drones will branch by your preference into offensive, defensive, repair and capture models.

Towers: Infantry, Mech and Wren can raise a tower for 1500 funds on plains, forest, hills or road. The builder becomes the tower's garrison and leaves the board as a separate piece: the army trades a unit for reach. A manned tower sees 3 hexes and can fire once a turn at range 2 with a mech-class shot, and enemies that strike it may be answered in kind. The garrison is safe while the tower stands; if the tower is destroyed, the garrison reappears on the hex at half strength, exhausted. Tap your tower and choose the leave icon to unman it: the garrison steps out whole and rested next turn, but an unmanned tower goes dormant, seeing only its own hex and unable to fire, until a friendly foot unit steps in and mans it again. An enemy foot unit standing on your tower captures it over two turns, just like a property; when the capture completes, the tower changes hands and any garrison inside is thrown out at half strength. Towers cannot be automated yet; that upgrade arrives with later battles.

The Ruin: the Old Ruin at the table's heart is more than scenery. Its ancient amber turret is alive: while the ruin is neutral it fires on anyone from either army who lingers in range 2–3. Infantry, Mech and Wren can capture the ruin like a property over two turns — stand on its hex beside the turret and choose Capture. Whoever holds the ruin gains +250 income a turn, and the turret changes allegiance with it, turning its guns on the holder's enemies. It can be re-captured the same way, and the turret flips with it. Its kills are credited to whoever holds it.

Veterans: units earn experience and rank chevrons (about +10% damage per rank) and keep a personal kill count, shown with a skull badge. Drone kills credit the shooter; tower kills credit the tower.

Forgiveness: a unit that has only moved can undo its move with the curved-arrow button that appears above it. A move that reveals new ground or a hidden enemy cannot be taken back. The battle saves itself as you play; resume it from the menu's Game section.

Inspecting the table: tap any hex and the readout card floating at the bottom shows that hex's terrain on the left and, when a unit or tower you can see stands there, its full details on the right; close it with its ✕ to return to the full map, or fold it to a slim strip with its ▾ chevron to peek underneath. If the hex you tap sits behind the card, the table pans itself just enough to bring it clear. The table is larger than the screen and drags to pan in every direction, even while the card is open; the menu (top-right) holds the objectives with live progress, sound settings, these rules, kill counts, the battle log and game controls, so the table itself stays clear.
